evals.prompt: What MCP tools does Directus expose? I just connected it and want to know what I can do with it
evals.expected_output: Lists all 12 MCP tools with their action patterns and the query system

assertions.text: Lists all 12 MCP tools by name
Mentions system-prompt tool as first call
Explains the unified action-based CRUD pattern
Mentions schema tool for discovery
Includes trigger-flow as a tool

evals.prompt: I'm calling the Directus items tool but getting 'action is required' error. What am I doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: Explains the unified action pattern and that every Directus MCP tool requires an action parameter

assertions.text: Identifies missing action parameter as the cause
Lists valid actions: create, read, update, delete
Shows correct JSON example with action parameter
Mentions data must be an array for create

evals.prompt: I need to read all published posts from my Directus with their author names, sorted by newest first, limit 10
evals.expected_output: Exact JSON for items tool with action:read, filter, dot notation fields, sort, limit

assertions.text: Uses action: read
Uses dot notation for author name (e.g. author.first_name or author.name)
Includes filter for status _eq published
Sorts by -date_created (descending)
Sets limit to 10

evals.prompt: How do I batch create 50 products in Directus? I have them in a list and want to insert them all
evals.expected_output: Data must be an array, batch in groups of 10-25, read schema first

assertions.text: Emphasizes data must be an array
Recommends batching in groups of 10-25 items
Advises reading schema first to know required fields
Shows JSON example with data array containing multiple items

evals.prompt: I want to build a blog CMS in Directus. What collections do I need and in what order should I create them?
evals.expected_output: Blog collections with creation order, system fields, display templates

assertions.text: Lists core collections: authors, categories, tags, posts, junction tables
Specifies creation order: independent first, then dependent, then junction
Mentions system fields (status, user_created, date_created)
Mentions display_template for item presentation
Shows MCP tool call examples

evals.prompt: What's the difference between schema: {} and schema: null when creating a Directus collection?
evals.expected_output: schema:{} = real table, schema:null = folder-only UI grouping

assertions.text: Explains schema:{} creates a real database table
Explains schema:null creates a folder-only collection (UI grouping, no table)
Shows JSON example for both cases

evals.prompt: How do I set up a many-to-many relation between posts and tags in Directus? I need the full step-by-step
evals.expected_output: Complete M2M workflow with junction collection, fields, alias fields, relations

assertions.text: Creates a junction collection (e.g. posts_tags) with hidden meta
Creates two uuid fields in junction (posts_id, tags_id)
Creates alias fields on both parent collections with list-m2m interface
Sets meta.special to m2m on alias fields
Creates relations with junction_field and one_field in meta
Uses CASCADE on_delete for junction relations

evals.prompt: What field type should I use for a featured image on my posts collection?
evals.expected_output: UUID type, file-image interface, special:[file], relation to directus_files

assertions.text: Specifies uuid type for the field
Uses file-image interface
Sets special to [file]
Creates relation to directus_files
Uses SET NULL on_delete

evals.prompt: Create a Directus flow that sends a Slack notification whenever a new post is published
evals.expected_output: Complete flow with event trigger, condition, request operation, correct syntax

assertions.text: Creates flow with event trigger on items.create or items.update for posts
Creates condition operation checking status equals published
Uses nested object syntax for condition filter (not dot notation)
Creates request operation with POST to Slack webhook
Uses array format for request headers [{header, value}]
Uses stringified JSON for request body
Connects operations via resolve and sets flow entry point

evals.prompt: How do I reference data from the trigger in a Directus flow operation?
evals.expected_output: Data chain variables: $trigger, payload, keys, operation_key references

assertions.text: Lists $trigger variable and sub-paths (payload, keys, collection)
Explains operation key references ({{ operation_key }})
Warns against using $last
Shows nested object syntax for condition filters
Mentions stringified JSON for request body

evals.prompt: I need to import a bunch of product images from URLs into Directus and organize them in a folder
evals.expected_output: Folders create, then files import with URL and metadata including folder UUID

assertions.text: Uses folders tool with create action first
Uses files tool with import action
Shows data as array with url and file metadata
Includes folder UUID in file metadata
Mentions batch import (multiple items in data array)

evals.prompt: How do I get the actual content of an image file from Directus for AI analysis?
evals.expected_output: Assets tool returns base64 content with mimeType

assertions.text: Identifies the assets tool (not files tool) for content retrieval
Shows input with id parameter
Mentions base64 encoded response
Mentions mimeType in response

evals.prompt: I need curl commands for Directus REST API — how do I list, create, and update items?
evals.expected_output: Curl examples for GET/POST/PATCH /items/{collection} with auth

assertions.text: Shows GET /items/{collection} for listing
Shows POST /items/{collection} for creating
Shows PATCH /items/{collection}/{id} for updating
Includes Authorization Bearer header
Shows query parameters (fields, filter, sort, limit)

evals.prompt: How do I do schema migrations between Directus environments?
evals.expected_output: 3-step pipeline: snapshot, diff, apply with curl examples

assertions.text: Describes 3-step pipeline: snapshot, diff, apply
Shows GET /schema/snapshot endpoint
Shows POST /schema/diff endpoint
Shows POST /schema/apply endpoint
Includes curl command examples with auth headers

evals.prompt: Show me how to set up the Directus SDK with TypeScript types and do basic CRUD
evals.expected_output: Composable client, TypeScript schema, readItems/createItem/updateItem/deleteItem

assertions.text: Uses createDirectus with composable pattern (rest, staticToken)
Shows TypeScript interface for schema
Shows readItems with fields and filter
Shows createItem example
Shows updateItem example
Uses correct imports from @directus/sdk

evals.prompt: How do I subscribe to real-time changes on a collection with the Directus SDK?
evals.expected_output: realtime() composable, connect(), subscribe(), for-await loop

assertions.text: Uses realtime() composable in client setup
Calls client.connect() before subscribing
Uses client.subscribe() with collection name and event type
Shows for-await-of loop for consuming events
Includes correct imports (createDirectus, realtime, staticToken)

evals.prompt: I'm getting 403 Forbidden when trying to create items via MCP in Directus. How do I fix this?
evals.expected_output: Role permissions, system collection permissions, MCP user permission table

assertions.text: Identifies insufficient role permissions as the cause
Points to Settings > Roles > Permissions
Lists system collections needing permissions (directus_collections, directus_fields, directus_relations)
Provides a permission table for MCP user minimum setup
Mentions checking both user collection and system collection permissions

evals.prompt: My Directus flow operations aren't executing even though the flow is active
evals.expected_output: Check flow.operation, resolve/reject chains, condition syntax, request format

assertions.text: Checks flow.operation field points to first operation UUID
Checks resolve/reject chains between operations
Warns about condition filter syntax (nested objects, not dot notation)
Mentions request body must be stringified JSON
Mentions request headers must be array of {header, value} objects

evals.prompt: Show me a complete example of building an e-commerce catalog in Directus from scratch
evals.expected_output: Full explore-build-populate workflow with MCP tool calls

assertions.text: Starts with schema discovery
Creates collections in correct dependency order
Includes products, categories, and variants collections at minimum
Sets up relationships (M2O, M2M)
Shows MCP tool call JSON examples

evals.prompt: I need to see what a typical Directus MCP tool call looks like — give me concrete JSON examples
evals.expected_output: Concrete JSON for schema, items, collections/fields tools

assertions.text: Shows schema tool JSON (discovery mode with empty input)
Shows items tool JSON with action and query
Shows collections or fields tool JSON with create action
All examples include Tool name and Input format
Includes at least 4 different tool examples
